fields.title: Enablement: no one reads manuals, so teach through the product
fields.keyTakeaway: Enablement works at the moment of the task and within the interface, not in advance or in a PDF. If a feature is not being used, first check whether people know about it and understand it — and only then add training.
fields.checkQuestion: 8% of users found a new feature. Which three reasons must be distinguished before writing a manual?
fields.blocks/0/text: Key node question: **how to teach users to reach their goals?**
fields.blocks/1/text: **What happens if you don't answer the question.** The release ends with a newsletter describing updates and a help center article. A month later, only a few use the feature, and the team concludes it isn't needed.
fields.blocks/2/subtitle: They require different fixes, so distinguish them before taking action
fields.blocks/2/items/0: **Don't know** — didn't see what was added. Fixed by a hint right where the task arises.
fields.blocks/2/items/1: **Don't understand** — saw it, didn't understand why or got scared. Fixed by naming it in the user's language and showing a result example.
fields.blocks/2/items/2: **Don't need** — understood and skipped. Can't be fixed with enablement; this is a signal about the solution, not the delivery.
fields.blocks/2/items/3: **How to distinguish:** look at whether they reach the screen, open it, and return a second time.
fields.blocks/3/text:
The "partial inventory" feature lets users scan a single shelf instead of the whole store. A month later, 8% use it.

Looking at the funnel: 46% open the screen, 11% start. So they know, but don't understand.

What was done: renamed it "Check single shelf" instead of "Partial inventory" and showed a hint right when the seller opened full inventory for the second time in a week.

A month later — 34%. Not a single help article was written.
fields.blocks/4/text: **For complex products, the champion role works.** In every store, there is a person who figured it out first; they are trained separately and referenced by others. This is cheaper than training everyone and lasts longer than a webinar.
fields.blocks/5/text: If you have to explain to people why a screen is needed, most often the problem is with the screen. Enablement amplifies what is clear; it does not replace design.
fields.blocks/5/title: Enablement won't save a bad solution
fields.blocks/6/text: In-product hints quickly become noise: three pop-ups in a row and everyone stops reading. Their budget is limited, and it should be spent at the moment of the task, not at the moment of release.
